title: Is AI Going To Be Bubble?
author: whatevervibestoday

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: both can be true. railways were a bubble and railways still changed everything, the people who lost were the ones paying peak prices for the build-out. what I watch is how much of the spending runs on debt instead of cash the business throws off.

replies.author: whatevervibestoday
replies.body: I agree I think AI will be profitable eventually, I have integrated it into my work and even sold AI based products. Are there any particular AI businesses you personally invest or would invest in?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: I mostly stay away from the model makers themselves, too much of the build-out runs on borrowed money for my taste. the power and cooling side gets paid whether or not any single app wins, so that's where I'd look first.

replies.author: whatevervibestoday
replies.body: That makes sense. Bet on the game not the players. What do you think about Elon having data centers in space?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: no idea on the timeline. the catch everyone skips is heat: space is cold but there's no air to carry it off, so the radiators end up enormous. I'd wait for one to actually run before paying for the story.

replies.author: whatevervibestoday
replies.body: I have practical concerns as well.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Nobody can say whether it's a bubble in advance, but a few measurable things separate a boom from a bubble: how much capital spending is being funded by debt or by circular deals between suppliers and customers, whether end-customer revenue is growing as fast as the spending, how concentrated the market is in a few names, and how valuations compare with earnings after a period of growth. Past technology cycles (railways, the late-1990s internet) had real, lasting technology and still produced large losses for investors who paid too much, so "the technology is real" and "prices are too high" can both be true. The scheduled data points are the earnings calls and capex announcements, and Event Cards at Cymetica are one place to look at event-based markets around them.

replies.author: whatevervibestoday
replies.body: Your spot on as far as I am concerned. My thoughts are about the short term. I think in the long term AI is a solid investment. I know there is a lot we simply cannot know.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks, and that split between a short-term worry and a long-term view is a sensible way to hold it, since the two can both be right. The earnings and capex dates are the checkpoints to watch on the short-term side.
